newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK LARGELY FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK LARGELY FIRMER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted firmer against most hard currencies with the exception of pound sterling at the close of Friday's interbank session which started off rather quietly but saw slightly more activity towards the end of the day.
"Early morning trading was fairly quiet but mid-morning we saw some selling, indicating that we had some inflows of foreign currency into the market," commented one dealer.
He said part of the money had come from the on-going annual tobacco sales while the rest was proceeds from horticultural exports.
But dealers say the latest surge in annual inflation, which went up to 22.4 percent in April from 19.9 percent in March, might soon start putting pressure on the local unit to depreciate.
"If we look at the fundamentals, there's now room for the Zimbabwe dollar to depreciate if we are to maintain our competitiveness against other currencies," one dealer said earlier in the week.

At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted half a cent firmer on the key U.S. dollar at 11.2950/3050 compared to 11.3000/3100 on Thursday and also gained ground on the mark to 6.6300/6500 from 6.6500/6570.
It was at 2.5150/5350 against the rand from 2.5210/5250 but however weakened against sterling to 18.5400/5600 from 18.5275/5540.
